credit.rationale: Ratings placed on Rating Watch with Developing Implications (RWD) pending clarity on the consolidated credit profile, following the announced scheme of amalgamation of AeroStructures Manufacturing India, Aequs Engineered Plastics and Aequs Force Consumer Products into Aequs. | Rating continues to factor in Aequs' established position in aerospace with full value-chain vertical integration and long-term agreements with reputed global customers (Airbus, Mattel), driving consistent order inflows. | Key monitorables are the gradual ramp-up/stabilisation of the large ATP consumer-electronics project and continuous net losses; liquidity is adequate, aided by the ~INR 814 crore raised via IPO/pre-IPO in Q3FY26 used for debt reduction.

deepdive.sec: Aerospace Precision Engineering & Consumer Electronics Contract Manufacturing

bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capacity expansion for confirmed customer demand (Mattel, Apple ecosystem); net debt/equity improved to 0.23x post-IPO; cash balance INR 3,015 Cr; no dividend mentioned, reinvestment mode for growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Consumer segment ramp-up delay beyond Q4FY27; dependency on single large consumer electronics customer; geopolitical supply chain disruptions (West Asia) impacting logistics and raw material lead times (Titanium 52 weeks, Steel 65-75 weeks); key management change (CFO stepping down); equipment sourcing constraints from China.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on long-term structural growth and moat (vertical integration, speed-to-market); transparent about short-term P&L pain from consumer capex; pragmatic on working capital buildup due to geopolitical stocking; committed to margin recovery via utilization.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% reported includes other income and excludes unallocated corporate costs; true operational margin is ~20%; Consumer electronics and Aerospace share 'precision manufacturing' platform capabilities but use distinct machine bases (CNC for metal/aero/electronics vs. Molding for plastics/toys); PLI benefits only start accruing in FY27.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital discipline is a core pillar of the Aequs Playbook, emphasizing upfront planning for ecosystem buildout, patience through long qualification cycles, and delayed operating leverage to achieve 20% steady-state ROCE by FY31.
- No dividend policy, balance sheet metrics, or specific reinvestment ratios are disclosed; the deck focuses on growth capex and breakeven milestones (Consumer EBITDA breakeven Q4FY27, Consolidated PAT breakeven H1FY28).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Aerospace: Revenue INR 10,464 Cr (+27% YoY), EBITDA INR 2,813 Cr (+76% YoY), ROCE 20%. Consumer: Revenue INR 1,840 Cr (+84% YoY), EBITDA Loss INR 783 Cr (loss widened due to new capacity commissioning); utilization currently 23%, targeting 40-50% in FY27.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain de-risking and China+1 strategy driving orders to India | Aequs Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of global OEMs shifting sourcing to India; unique position with vertically integrated capabilities and large order book. |
| Raw material inflation and logistics disruption | Indian Aerospace Suppliers without long-term contracts | loser | Med | Players without pass-through mechanisms or long-term material coverage will suffer margin compression from titanium/steel price spikes and logistics delays. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- India's first and only vertically integrated aerospace manufacturer, with a single-campus ecosystem (Forging → Machining → Surface Treatment → Assembly) that reduces part travel from 5,000 km to under 500 meters, creating the lowest carbon footprint per part.
- Differentiated value proposition built on institutional repeatability, risk compression at scale, and an ecosystem multiplier model that co-locates partners and shared infrastructure, driving >50% Cluster Value Add (CVA).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Listing] Aequs Limited was listed on NSE (AEQUS) and BSE (544634) on December 10, 2025, marking its entry into public markets.
- [JV Partnerships] Key joint ventures include SQuAD (50:50 with Aubert & Duval for closed-die forging), API (50:50 with Magellan Aerospace for surface treatment), ACPL (50:50 with Tramontina for premium cookware), and Ajna Aerospace & Defence (equal JV with Accel India and Vagus Defence for UAVs).
- [Awards/Trust] Multiple OEM awards (Airbus Innovation Award 2016, Ramp-up Champion 2024, Boeing Premier Bidder 2022) and first-in-India certifications (Airbus & Boeing approved surface treatment) serve as durable credentials for regulatory trust and customer preference.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Revenue: INR 12,304 Cr (+33% YoY); EBITDA: INR 1,545 Cr (+43% YoY, 13% margin); PAT: Loss of INR 1,133 Cr (improved from -11% to -9% margin); Order Book: $889 Mn (Aerospace only); Net Debt/Equity: 0.23x. One-offs/Distortions: Q4 PAT loss of INR 541 Cr driven by full run-rate depreciation on new consumer capex before utilization ramped; Aerospace segment EBITDA margin of 27% includes other income, operational margin guided at 20%.
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: Aerospace margins sustained at ~20% operational level despite mix changes; Consumer margins depressed by low utilization (23%) and high fixed depreciation; material cost inflation (titanium/steel) passed through to customers via long-term agreements; logistics costs up slightly due to West Asia crisis but deemed non-material.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: FY27 Revenue Growth: 45-50% consolidated (Aerospace 25-30%, Consumer 125-150%); Margins: Aerospace ~20% EBITDA, Consumer to reach EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27; Order Inflow: Continued addition of 100+ SKUs/quarter in Aerospace; Capex: INR 660 Cr total (INR 160 Cr Aerospace, INR 500 Cr Consumer).
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: $889 million in Aerospace (approx. 8-9x trailing aerospace revenue); robust visibility driven by 433 new parts added in Q4 alone (total portfolio 5,654 SKUs); long-term agreements with global OEMs for engine and landing gear components.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New INR 1,900 Cr MoU for vertically integrated aero-engine/landing gear park in Hosur (Tamil Nadu); INR 2,856 Cr expansion in Belagavi/Hubballi; moving up value chain into engine components (revenue impact from FY28); PLI scheme eligibility starting FY27.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Aequs delivered a landmark FY26 with 33% revenue growth and a $889M aerospace order book, but consolidated PAT remains negative due to aggressive consumer electronics capex depreciation. The investment thesis hinges on achieving consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4FY27 and sustaining 20%+ aerospace margins as new Hosur and Karnataka capacities commission.

open.item: Most FY26 capex already done; no significant new capex expected this year, only some capitalization spilling into Q4 (mainly consumer electronics).
CFO Dinesh Iyer to step down at end of June 2026 for personal reasons; Harish Bang to be interim single point of contact while a replacement is sought.
Consumer segment EBITDA to hit break-even by Q4 FY27, a major inflection for consolidated profitability.
No PLI income booked in FY26; FY27 will be the first year Aequs is eligible for PLI incentives.
FY27 planned consumer capex of approximately INR 500 crores, on top of ~INR 830 crore existing consumer gross block.
FY27 planned aerospace capex of approximately INR 160 crores.
Drive consumer capacity utilisation from 23% today to a target of 40% to 50% by FY27 year-end.
FY27 capex (~INR 660 crores combined) to be funded via a mix of debt/borrowings and internal accruals; interest cost expected to reduce YoY.
FY27 consumer revenue growth of about 125% to 150%, predominantly driven by consumer electronics.
Project doubling operational EBITDA in FY27 on operating leverage.
FY27 consolidated top-line revenue growth of approximately 45% to 50%.
FY27 aerospace revenue to grow 25% to 30% with segment EBITDA margins maintained at 20%.
Pre-IPO guidance for overall PAT-positive by end of FY27 is being re-evaluated; management declined to reaffirm the timeline pending consumer electronics capacity decisions.
Consolidated PAT expected to reach break-even by H1 FY28; PAT to stay negative for much of FY27 due to heavy depreciation.
Engine components not material in FY27; revenue expected to start flowing from FY28 onward.
Consumer electronics to reach ~1.5x asset turn at peak utilisation, implying ~INR 2,000 crore revenue potential (INR 830cr + INR 500cr gross block), targeted closer to CY2029.
Consumer steady-state EBITDA margins of 18-20% expected once utilisation reaches ~75-80%.
Signed long-term agreement with Mattel; both sides committed to scaling volumes, expected to absorb Hasbro capacity impact.
Hasbro informed Aequs it revised its sourcing strategy and will stop raising POs; management says Mattel long-term agreement will absorb the capacity impact.
Signed second MoU (Mar 2026) with Karnataka committing INR 2,856 crores over five years across Belagavi and Hubballi clusters (aerospace precision + consumer capacity).

wtt.summary: Building track record — 2Q logged, no reconciled verdicts yet.
wtt.tone_latest: Confident and specific with quantified FY27 guidance across both segments; management owned the consumer EBITDA drag and the Q4 margin compression, and was transparent about the Hasbro loss and CFO departure while framing them as manageable.
